stories.title: Figure brings its F.03 humanoid robots to the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix with T-Mobile
paragraphs: Figure said on X on Nov. 20, 2026, that it is partnering with T-Mobile to bring its F.03 humanoid robots to the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix "this weekend." HumanoidMegaHub notes the race weekend runs Nov. 19 to 21, and reports that Figure has not said what the robots will do there, how many will attend, or whether they will interact directly with fans.

According to HumanoidMegaHub, the appearance builds on an existing relationship between the two companies. The outlet reports that T-Mobile announced in April 2026 that Figure's F.03 robots were being designed to connect to its 5G Advanced network, and that T-Mobile CTO John Saw wrote in October that the work "began with connectivity: eSIM service for Figure AI's humanoid robots."

HumanoidMegaHub reports that T-Mobile and Figure are now evaluating whether parts of Figure's Helix S1 and S2 AI models could run on computing at the network edge instead of entirely on the robot. The outlet adds that neither company has confirmed the Las Vegas appearance will involve testing edge AI or other advanced network features, and that Figure has already deployed F.03 robots in industrial settings, including BMW manufacturing operations.

stories.title: FDA clears Medtronic's Hugo surgical robot for general surgery in the U.S.
paragraphs: Medtronic announced this week that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has cleared its Hugo robotic-assisted surgery system for general surgery, The Robot Report reports. The clearance covers all upper abdominal general surgery procedures, including gallbladder removal, Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, ventral hernia repair and small bowel resection, plus inguinal hernia repair and appendix removal. Medtronic says these procedures add up to about 3.5 million surgeries a year in the U.S.

Hugo is a modular, cart-based system that lets surgeons use only the robotic arms a procedure needs. According to The Robot Report, it gained FDA approval for urology in December 2025 and received CE marking for general surgery in Europe in 2022. Medtronic says Hugo is on track to pass 50,000 procedures worldwide by the end of its fiscal year.

Rajit Kamal, Medtronic's general manager of robotic surgical technologies, told The Robot Report the company combined a U.S. clinical trial with data from outside the U.S. to win a broader set of general surgery uses. Medtronic is also running a U.S. study of Hugo for hysterectomies, and in September it invested $700 million in Cornerstone Robotics, the outlet reports.

stories.title: MassRobotics is building a marine robot testing site on Boston Harbor
paragraphs: MassRobotics is developing a marine robotics facility at the Boston Fish Pier, where startups will be able to build, launch and test robots in Boston Harbor, The Robot Report reports. Construction is underway in partnership with the Massachusetts Port Authority. Programs are planned to start during 2027, and the facility is set to open in early 2028.

According to the report, the site will have a water tank, a float next to the pier for testing directly in the water, and lifting and launch equipment for moving vehicles in and out of the harbor. MassRobotics supports more than 100 resident startups.

"Marine startups tell us that finding a place to test is one of their biggest hurdles," MassRobotics executive director Tom Ryden said. One of its marine startups, CRABI Robotics, makes an underwater robot that cleans ship hulls.
